tips.comment: This well-bred C Appleby-trained colt made a promising racecourse debut over six furlongs on good to firm ground at Haydock when only beaten 1 1/4 lengths in second behind his stablemate Maximized. So, with that run under his belt, he can go one place better today under the retained jockey W Buick.
Best run to date when third at Windsor on his handicap debut last month. Hit trouble in running so can succeed here off the same mark if getting a clearer run.

Four runs this year for the 3yo filly, consistent form. She was only beaten 3L in a £34K Listed contest three weeks ago - meeting a bit of trouble in the race. Her handicap mark of 73 is looking very attractive after that effort.

This horse caught my eye last time on handicap debut where he was held up in the last trio. Going well, he moved through horses but came up short in 6th. Today, he steps up to the mile, which looks perfect, and Rossa Ryan retains the ride, which is a pointer for the top-class Clive Cox team.

Consecrated looked very special on her first run at this track, using her long stride to win comfortably in a race that has worked out well. She then was only 4th in a listed race at York but that race has thrown up some good horses and she seemed to get caught out by the fast ground. Back on a softer surface she should bounce back to win this. Blue Bolt is the obvious danger and she looked pretty useful at Windsor last time.
Good start when 3rd of 5 on debut. Step up in trip to 1m should suit on pedigree, and top trainer William Haggas does well here with 3-year-old horses. Solid each-way player.
On a hat-trick of wins if successful here. Won by 4 lengths over this distance last week, and the weight penalty for that is negated by the jockey's 5lb claim. Most highly rated horse in the field.
Previous distance winner. A very solid 2nd at Brighton last time out and up 3 lb for that run, but still looks open to improvement. So should make a bold bid here.

Unplugged has been dropped 10 lbs in his last 5 runs. Three of them were on the all-weather, which does suit, and his comeback run where he was probably in need of the run. Last time at Haydock, he looked like the winner 2f out before his effort flattened out. He drops back 2f here, which looks like a plus. He ran well on his only start at the track and is 6 lbs below his last winning mark.

Raced well to win at Southwell after a gelding operation, and didn't do too badly when beaten by a head at Carlisle after returning from a 182-day break. Expected to run better this time around, now fitter, and has a huge jockey booking in William Buick on board.

Believe The Storm ran a very nice race first time out to finish second to a promising sort at Kempton and can win this on his first attempt in a handicap for charismatic owner Basher Watts and trainer Charlie Fellowes.

Hickory won a big field competitive Class 2 handicap at Ascot on penultimate start and had excuses last time out at Sandown. Happy to draw a line through that, and this is a drop in class. He looks a solid each way bet with the extra place.

Quite a competitive class 3 with several in with a shout, but the one I've sided with is the unexposed Tom Clover 4yo Surrey Shadow. Only 6 starts to date, winning once and placed twice. Didn't see out the stiff Sandown mile last time, so the step back to this flat Newbury 7f should be ideal.

Ex Aidan O’Brien trained 4yo. He had a mark of 90 when making his debut for this UK yard last year, now racing off a tempting 72 rating. He struggled last year but was much improved five weeks ago on quick turf ground after coming back from a break. He was a good 3rd of 12 that day, over this 7f trip, seeing the race out nicely. The runner-up that day has won twice since and rated much higher now. Every chance the selection can improve for that run.
20/1 and a reasonable 6th of 18 on debut, but that looks like a good start on paper. Over this slightly further trip should suit and solid each way chance here on a flat track.

Arnaz has been sent off at short prices for his last 3 starts and has probably been better than the result on a couple of occasions. He's still only 4 and could have some upside to him. His SPs suggest that he's capable off this mark. He ran his best race in a 17-runner handicap at Haydock, so it could be that a big field suits him, and he looks worth an interest.

Very surprised to see Tulip at 12/1, so I will take that, thank you. Got her own way in front and made it count when winning nicely at Windsor last time, and that was a career-best. Three of her top runs have come when able to dominate, so tactics will be key again. Still fairly treated after just a 5lb rise. If allowed to stride on, she's a live EW/WIN player.

A very open sprint handicap where Rocking Ends appeals. He steps up in trip and looks a likely improving sort. He has steadily dropped in the weights and ran well last time at Goodwood off a higher mark.

This horse absolutely hacked up in a maiden here on debut, and she makes her 4-year-old debut here today. So this could be the best time to catch her. She was then pitched straight into the 1000 Guineas, where she was admittedly outclassed but was in the same price bracket as horses rated 100-110. So I think a handicap off 83 could be well within her compass. The stable jockey is booked for the first time, and the horse is thoroughly exposed.

Talented individual who doesn't always put his best foot forward, as he didn't when well beaten at Windsor last time. He is lurking on a dangerous mark though, so it would be no surprise to see him run well this afternoon.
Weakened a furlong out over the extended 7 furlongs at Lingfield last month and should welcome the drop in trip, being three times a winner over 6 furlongs, twice off higher marks than today.
Makes his turf debut. Opening mark looks a good one to work with, and over a stiff flat track, he can make a good turf debut. Top trainer does well at Yarmouth.

Veteran, who hasn't won for a while, has been slipping down the weights and showed signs of a revival when 2nd over course and distance last month. Really poor last time, so needs to put that well behind him, but will surely be striking off this sort of mark soon.

A previous course and distance winner, however, has been a bit down lately. Weight is dropping back to a near workable mark, and a chance is taken here as he may not be ready to strike but can go close. So basically, he is very capable on his day and nicely treated on older form, but needs to bounce back in a big way. Each-way chance if rediscovering his mojo.

A beaten favourite when headed close to home and runner-up over 7 furlongs at Brighton on Monday but travelled strongly for a long way. Turned round quickly for this, remains on the same mark and should welcome the drop in trip.
Previous course and distance winner this time last year and is now on a 9lb lower mark. Has slipped to a very handy mark and top jockey Silvestre de Sousa takes over the ride. Each way player.
Kept on to go fourth over 6 furlongs on the Lingfield polytrack last week and worth a look on turf dropping in trip and class.

The 4yo filly looks a little overpriced in this 5f handicap. Just 5 career runs. She ran a nice race on her return early May after coming off an 8 month break, up with the pace for a long way and only beaten just over a length. She was up against some capable race fit rivals that day, the winner has run a couple of decent races since. She won’t need much improvement to be a player at this low level.

Bernard is now just one pound above his last winning mark. He is a reliable type at this trip with 7 wins over the minimum distance and is very effective in blinkers and tongue strap. He did need his return run at Wolverhampton and is back down to a workable mark for me to get interested here. Each-way if fit and ready.
Free Pic is making its debut in a handicap race. It ran quite well at Catterick in April, coming sixth. It was disappointing last time but was drawn wide at Chester. It can improve on that.

This W J Haggas-trained 3-year-old colt has finished a close second in his last two races, both over seven furlongs. The latest was at Newbury when only beaten a head behind the J Ferguson-trained Montpellier. So with Cieran Fallon doing the steering, he looks hard to oppose today.

0-16 but seems to have found his level and went close off this mark at Beverley last month. A bit below that level last time, but the visor goes on and really ought to be capable of breaking his duck soon.

Lightly raced 3yo, three runs this year and was a good winner three weeks ago after switching back to turf. It was his first run over this 14f trip. He picked up nicely when asked for an effort, never really in trouble in the final furlong - decent yardstick in second - the pair had pulled well clear of the rest. More to come from this one.

Back from a break with two runs for a new yard last month. Excuses for the 6yo last time out, but he was a good 3rd in his previous race and that form is working out very nicely. He has been rated quite a bit higher in the past. He had the rival ‘A Major Payne’ behind in 5th that day and that runner is a short price for this handicap.

This horse has been placed an incredible 7 times (winning one) over C&D, so it's somewhat surprising that we get an e/w price on him here in this really weak race. A look through his career runs also shows that he has a good record at this time of year, with June in particular being a month when he runs his most competitive races. Looks like he'll be hard to keep out of the frame here, I would suggest.

This G Elliott-trained 4-year-old filly won on her racecourse debut in a two-mile NHF race on good ground at Cork 33 days ago. She stayed on well to beat the E Bolger-trained Samba Train by 1 3/4 lengths. With Mr. H C Swan taking a valuable three pounds off, she can make her trip from Ireland worthwhile.

The Gordon Elliott favorite looks the obvious one, but the form doesn't amount to much. The Olly Murphy-trained Princess Milania has shown a very good level of form in Irish point-to-points, particularly a second to the very useful Tom George import, Heron In The Park.

The addition of headgear seems to have worked the oracle for Dirty Den. Five-pound claimer here, and Anthony Charlton has the horse in top order with a win and a second in this preparation since resumption.

I did this last time, where it was truly terrible. However, I did mention that the cheekpieces were missing, so perhaps the time has finally come for the horse to come good. The Flemensfirth gelding is 28lb lower than last year's triumph at Fontwell, and I just can't help but feel it has been plotted.

The model I run suggests Kitesurfer should win this one. Kitesurfer lines up here with a comparably high RPR in what looks like a tightly bunched race. Kitesurfer lines up with a kinder official ranking and looks well treated off this market. Over a stone less than the top weight and 5-7 lbs lighter than the other main market contenders. Kitesurfer is the only one to have shown form of late with figures of 171-3 and is the only one who has won prior course and distance. Joe Anderson picks up the reins and relieves a further 3 lbs off the weight, taking Kitesurfer to be net the lowest weight out there for the 2m 7f trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Back from a 706-day break. Useful Irish horse back in 2023. Comes here on a good mark of 132 and also joins a top UK trainer. Might well be overlooked on stable debut.
Janworth was cruising to victory a couple of days ago before she fell at the last. Joe Anderson rides again. Now with 11st 8lbs on this mares back she should go extremely well here.

Cable Bay mare who should probably start favourite given that she's on the improve in this role and returned to win under Harry Skelton last time out. Course and distance winner and looks to have plenty of upside.

The model I run suggests Hello Cello can cause an upset here. Hello Cello lines up with the highest RPR on offer in this 8-horse race and does not look overly penalized for it in the weights. Other main market contenders carry a similar load and Ciaran O'Shea claims 7 lbs off Hello Cello's back. A good second last time out on this course in May and looks to get one better from that. Was racing in a class above this until very recently, so this should represent an opportunity to get back over the line first. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

McGregor's Charge runs here off a very attractive RPR compared to the rest of the field. Also carries less weight than the rest of the field. Looks attractive from all points and raced 7 days ago, so there shouldn't be any issues over being race ready! Serious contender.

The model I run suggests Hold Your Fort can win this one. Hold Your Fort lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 10-runner field but has an official ranking closer to the lower order. This subsequently results in Hold Your Fort carrying less weight around this 2m 7f class 3 chase. Showed excellent progression to win the 3m 2f class 3 handicap chase on 28th May and looks to repeat proceedings here. De Teller's fortune represents stiffer competition but has been pulled up twice out of the last 5 outings. Siding with the reliability of Hold Your Fort. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Won over 3 miles at Uttoxeter last month and the runner-up, Imperial Alex, boosted the form when winning at Perth on Sunday.
Placed in good ground Bangor bumper in April and made a solid start to hurdling when 2nd of 15 at Tipperary last month. Each way player here.
Twice raced 3yo, placed at Kempton on debut in April, placed at ChC last time out. Both runs at 8f, up in trip will suit. Yard in good form, Oisin Murphy in sparkling form.
3-year-old Churchill gelding, 3 runs this year going off as favorite twice, and placed twice. Up from 8f to 10f should suit. Must go well for the Balding/Murphy duo.
Fourth at Naas last time out, returning from a five and a half months break. Had been in good form prior to that run and sure to strip fitter here.

Forgive the latest run where blinkers didn't help at The Curragh. Generally reliable and has the form for this trip, including a win. Returns to a more suitable test now and is still well treated by the handicapper, so each-way player if bouncing back.

Gritty winner over 10f at Navan two runs ago and not disgraced when sixth last time out, only beaten around 3 lengths. She’s up in trip now and has won on this sort of ground before, but might be nudging the ceiling of her mark. So, as she is a reliable type, she could sneak into the frame if stamina holds. Each-way shout.

I have lost track of the number of trainers El Bello has had over the years, but he is currently with Denis Hogan, for whom he had his third and latest win over seven furlongs at Dundalk last year. He could defy top weight because he is now down to a career-low mark of 59. He might be able to defy top weight in this competitive affair. Third on two starts at the Curragh earlier this season, he did well to finish seventh when drawn widest of all on his penultimate outing at this venue. He could be ready to go in today.

Prince does tend to run freely and did too much too soon last time out over a mile at Gowran. Not the most consistent and yet to win in 29 tries, but has placed in similar company. Distance is a question mark for me, but if settling better, could nick a minor spot. Each-way if back to previous form.
